summary: Phased return: staged laptop handback, SAML reprovision, and conditional KMS access for returning engineer
description:
Background: A former IC (internal candidate) is scheduled to return from a 6-month leave on 2026-03-22. HR requested a phased reprovisioning: network-limited access on day 1, full access after manager confirmation, and temporary KMS key access for a 48-hour data-recovery window. The employee will first be local to the EU region for onboarding week 1 then relocate to US after week 2.

Request: Confirm recommended safe workflow for staged account reactivation, SAML assertion re-provisioning across identity providers, device staging (loaner vs full laptop), and controlled KMS access that automatically revokes after the window. HR wants an approval checklist and automation recommendations to minimize manual steps.

Impact: If done incorrectly, there is risk of over-privileged access (KMS/data exposure) or blocking the engineer from recovering critical artifacts. This is time-sensitive; HR needs the runbook and automation before 2026-03-18.

Context: Previously we handled similar one-off returns manually (see INT-46209 and INT-27133) with device handback and KMS handoff. This case differs because the employee will be remote and cross-region for the first two weeks and requires a temporal KMS grant tied to an SRE-approved recovery job.

Desired outcome: 1) A clear step-by-step runbook HR can use that includes checklist items and approval gates. 2) An automated or semi-automated process (ServiceNow/Jira/Okta workflow) to create a time-limited KMS grant bound to a specific repo/artifact path. 3) Device staging plan: loaner shipped immediately with VPN-only access until manager signs off, then full laptop shipped or local pickup.

Requested deliverables: runbook in Confluence, an Okta SAML group template for staged access, and a short playbook for SRE to issue and revoke the KMS grant with audit links.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - procedural request rather than reproducible bug

Simulate reprovision flow for a returning employee by creating a staged account in Okta with limited groups, issuing a timeboxed KMS grant scoped to 'projects/recovery/INT-887550/*', and confirming access from an EU-hosted workstation
Verify that KMS grant automatically revokes after 48 hours and that log entries appear in CloudTrail/KMS audit with principal and session tags

investigation_notes: Checked prior runbooks: INT-46209 contains KMS handback steps but lacks JIT automation and cross-region considerations.
Okta: confirmed we have ability to script group membership changes via SCIM; recommended approach is a 'staged-return' group mapped to limited roles.
KMS: security policy requires principal tagging and tight resource ARN scope. Identified 'projects/recovery/INT-887550/*' as acceptable temporary scope for the recovery job.
Device provisioning options: loaner laptop + corporate VPN only OR full laptop with disk encryption and MDM. Loaner preferred for initial remote start to reduce immediate inventory changes.
resolution_notes: Work in progress. Agreed approach: 1) Create Confluence runbook draft (DEV-PR-3784) with approval gates. 2) Okta staged group template 'staged_return_standard' created and will be tested in staging. 3) SRE to deploy lambda JIT KMS grant; automation will tag grants with 'INT-887550' and auto-revoke after 48 hours. Manager sign-off required to escalate to full access. Expected completion and handoff to HR by 2026-03-17.
